title: Modified percutaneous Achilles tenotomy according to Hoke for the minimally invasive treatment of pes cavus – a retrospective analysis of safety and efficacy compared with alternative ‘open’ procedures
summary:
In the field of paediatric neuro-orthopaedics, there are numerous surgical procedures available for the treatment of structural pes equinus. This is defined as a foot deformity characterised by dorsiflexion of the ankle joint (AJ) that is less than the neutral position (1). The main soft tissue structures affected are the shortened calf muscles (gastrocnemius, soleus), possibly with additional contracture of the dorsal capsular components of the ankle joint. Surgical treatment essentially involves lengthening these structurally shortened structures.
The standard procedure for surgical treatment of pes cavus in the Department of Paediatric and Neuro-Orthopaedics at the Clinic and Polyclinic for Orthopaedics and Trauma Surgery is a modified version of the percutaneous Achilles tenotomy according to Hoke (which essentially concerns the post-operative management). This is a minimally invasive procedure first described in 1942 by Hatt and Lamphier (2), which appears to offer advantages over other established procedures in terms of invasiveness and the extent and duration of post-operative care. Open Z-plasty remains widely used in German-speaking countries.
As part of a PhD thesis, the Hoke procedures carried out in the Paediatric and Neuro-Orthopaedics Section between 2016 and 2025 are to be retrospectively analysed in terms of their effectiveness and safety. A survey covering the period from 2016 to 2018 identified just over 100 cases (3). The planned study is expected to involve many times this number of cases.
The study is being conducted in cooperation with the Medical Service of North Rhine-Westphalia (MD). The key parameters (incision-to-suture times, length of hospital stay, complication rates, etc.) will be compared with the data available to the MD on open procedures (in particular the Z-plasty, which is widely used in German-speaking countries (1, 4)) and evaluated in summary.

Bibliography:
1.	Döderlein L, Wenz W, Schneider U. Fußdeformitäten: Der Spitzfuß/der Hackenfuß: Springer-Verlag; 2013.
2.	Hatt RN, Lamphier TA. Triple hemisection: a simplified procedure for lengthening the Achilles tendon. New England Journal of Medicine. 1947;236(5):166-9.
3.	Struwe C, Bornemann R, Plöger MM, Koob S, Kasapovic A, Hackenberg R, et al. [Modified percutaneous achillotentomy according to Hoke for minimally invasive treatment of pointed foot]. Oper Orthop Traumatol. 2021.
4.	Döderlein L. Infantile Zerebralparese.  Infantile Zerebralparese: Diagnostik, konservative und operative Therapie: Springer; 2015. p. 39-95.
conditions: structural pes equinus resulting from neuromuscular disorders

interventions.name:
1. Planning and compiling a comprehensive table containing all measured values, and conducting an extensive literature review
2. Retrospective collection of all previously defined parameters from electronic patient records
3. Retrospective collection of the previously defined comparison parameters

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
percutaneous Achilles tenotomy performed according to the Hoke method during the follow-up period
Exclusion criteria:
Incorrect coding / Inability to collect data retrospectively
